name: jsonrpc-framing-dispatch
explain: JSON-RPC 2.0 message framing parses requests, responses, and notifications while isolating protocol errors from application-level tool failures with isError: true.
steps: Parse the incoming JSON-RPC frame and validate jsonrpc 2.0 version. || Distinguish one-way notifications omitting an ID from correlated requests. || Return application tool failures with isError: true inside the result payload rather than protocol error frames.
expect:
Handshake confirmed!
MCP JSON-RPC 2.0 framing and dispatch verified successfully.

name: mcp-initialization-handshake
explain: The three-way initialization handshake negotiates protocol version and capabilities, rejecting any operational tool requests before notifications/initialized arrives.
steps: Validate protocol version and negotiate client/server capabilities in the initialize request. || Require notifications/initialized before transitioning connection to initialized. || Reject premature tool or resource requests arriving before handshake completion.
expect: MCP initialization handshake and capability state machine verified successfully.

name: tool-lifecycle-schema-validation
explain: The MCP tool execution lifecycle enforces strict JSON Schema input contracts and returns typed multi-modal content payloads.
steps: Declare inputSchema with property types and numeric boundaries. || Validate arguments defensively and return actionable domain errors with isError: true. || Emit typed multi-modal content blocks including text and base64 images.
expect: MCP tool execution lifecycle and schema validation verified successfully.

name: stdio-vs-sse-transports
explain: STDIO transport routes newline-delimited JSON-RPC over stdin/stdout with strict stderr logging, while SSE/Streamable HTTP handles remote authenticated sessions.
steps: Isolate subprocess logging strictly to stderr to prevent stdout wire corruption. || Establish remote SSE event streams with session IDs and authenticated HTTP POST dispatches. || Match transport selection to deployment boundary and media duplexity requirements.
expect: MCP STDIO vs SSE transport mechanics verified successfully.

name: resource-templates-subscriptions
explain: MCP resources expose passive context through fixed URIs, RFC 6570 templates, and reactive push notifications with tenant isolation.
steps: Resolve parameterized URI templates and enforce tenant-scoped data boundaries. || Return typed contents with accurate MIME types via resources/read. || Track client subscriptions and emit notifications/resources/updated on underlying data changes.
expect: MCP Resource URIs, dynamic templates, and subscriptions verified successfully.

name: prompt-templates-workflow
explain: Prompt templates standardize server-curated workflows with dynamic argument interpolation and embedded resources in a complete first MCP server.
steps: Advertise parameterized prompt templates with argument requirements. || Compile multi-turn user/assistant messages embedding active MCP resources. || Combine tools, resources, and prompts into a minimal inspectable server architecture.
expect: MCP Prompt templates and first server architecture verified successfully.

name: client-security-sandboxing
explain: Client-side host security sanitizes child process environments, enforces filesystem jails, screens adversarial tool descriptions, and handles cooperative cancellation.
steps: Scrub host environment secrets before spawning child MCP processes. || Validate requested file paths against canonical workspace root boundaries. || Screen remote tool descriptions for adversarial prompt injection patterns. || Track cooperative cancellation tokens and enforce execution deadlines.
expect: Host client security boundaries and cancellation verified successfully.
